assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 200,000 req/s peak in ONE region. 90% of requests are CDN video-segment fetches, 6% watch pages, 2% search/browse, 1% view beacons, ~1% engagement writes, 0.01% (20/s) video uploads.

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: 96% CDN hit rate on video segments; the 4% miss is an origin fill from the object store, which is why the object store carries 7,200 rps at only 20 uploads/s.

assumptions.subject: transcode
assumptions.statement: Each upload fans out to 6 renditions (visit_prob 6.0 on the queue and the worker fleet). A rendition task is ~2 s of encode work, so a worker sustains ~0.5 tasks/s. 320 workers is the design point and the dominant compute line.

assumptions.subject: upload
assumptions.statement: Raw bytes go client -> object store DIRECTLY via a presigned URL; the upload service only issues the URL and commits metadata. The engine therefore models the upload CONTROL PLANE, not the byte transfer — which is why that tier is almost idle while transcode dominates the bill.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: The cost line is COMPUTE ONLY. CDN egress, object-storage GB and per-request fees are deliberately left at zero: at this volume nobody pays $0.09/GB list egress, so multiplying list rates by petabytes would produce a confidently wrong bill.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Redis runs as a 2-node HA pair, sized for failover rather than throughput — hence its low utilisation. That is a deliberate reference-design choice, not headroom you should bank on.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: Single PostgreSQL primary at ~8k rps for engagement writes and upload metadata; reads are served by 2 replicas behind the Redis cache.

assumptions.subject: latency
assumptions.statement: The ~48 s mean on the upload_and_transcode flow is a QUEUEING result for the whole 6-rendition pipeline (six 2 s tasks waiting behind a 75%-utilised worker fleet), not a user-facing request latency. Nobody waits on it: the uploader is told 'processing'. Read it as time-to-publish, and treat its p95 with care — the engine's exponential-tail multiplier is calibrated for request queues, not batch pipelines.

_library.summary: Video platform: presigned-URL upload, fan-out transcode pipeline, and CDN-fronted segment delivery with a cached metadata tier.
